bandeira-randomstrasse-problem-11-comple.why: Matches the record's identification: r·x = n − 2d(r,x), so disc(A) ≥ v exactly when the rows and their complements cover the cube within radius (n−v)/2, which gives D_n = n − 2ρ_n. The draft says 'at most 2n' codewords where the record says 'size 2n'. These are equivalent: repeated rows or complementary row pairs give fewer than 2n distinct codewords, and a smaller complement-closed code can be padded with complement pairs without raising the covering radius, since 2^n ≥ 2n. The parity condition on v is implicit in the record because r·x ≡ n (mod 2). Both K(n,R) consequences (K ≤ n certifies D_n ≥ n−2R; K > 2n rules it out) are stated as in the record. The proof text is the record verbatim. It is labelled unrefereed and author checked, consistent with the record's status.
